_what: Every place on this Mac the Trillion app looks for, the first time it opens and on every launch after (computer-sources.mjs beside it), and how each is read (read-new-items.mjs). A program row with a `resident` (a hearing row, `know_who`) is kept running with its model loaded (computer/resident.py, started with `resident.run` on `resident.socket` when nothing answers there, ending itself after `idle_seconds` unasked), so a model is loaded once rather than once per piece. One list for every program that reads a computer: the Trillion helper (read-this-computer.mjs, started by wake-sessions.mjs) and the Trillion Mac app, which imports this file. `{program}` in a switch's words is the program macOS lists for it. A row says what the place is, where it lives and how to check it; a row with a `listen` block (the listening row) is the microphone, heard by listen.mjs while its `switch` file says on: `capture` opens the microphone once and keeps it open while listening is on, writing a piece of `piece_seconds` after piece into `{folder}` and printing one `<file>,<start>,<end>` line as each finishes (opening it again for every piece made macOS's sound server build and tear down a recording every half minute), the first `hearing` row hears it, `know_who` names who said each part against the people enrolled in `people` (know-who.py; its `voices` say how alike counts as one voice, and a voice heard for less than `new_voice_shortest_seconds` joins the voice it is most like instead of starting one), a moment ends after `moments.quiet_seconds` quiet, a listener started within `moments.same_session_within_seconds` of the last one goes on with its session (so an unknown voice keeps its number), `rules` over each turn's words, speaker (me, enrolled, unknown), name and text leave turns out, `pause_when_said` turns it off, and every kept turn goes to the one door under `route` as its speaker's message; a place nobody listed yet is one more row. Each recording a drive's keeper sends is also seen at capture by the first `seeing` row whose program answers its `check` (see-a-recording.mjs): its still, strip of frames and waveform are kept as the file's preview, sized by the row's `sizes` (the browser maker's sizes), so nothing else decodes it. `look` names a way of checking (paths, entries, browser_sites) and its places; a `paths` look may read `facts` about what it found (`file` under it, `keys` from that property list, plus `path`) and pick the first of its `works` rules whose every `if` test holds (`contains` text, `at_least` / `below` a dotted version) for the place's `detail` (with {fact} filled in) and, when the rule says `carries`, the row's `carries` service (a service-connections vendor) is carried by this computer: `carrier` is the one card the computer publishes naming each such service as a skill, renewed every look, so Connections shows it Connected; `gate` names the switch macOS asks for before the place can be read (`gates`: its `open` pane address, its `guide` address that the Trillion app answers with a panel beside System Settings holding the app's icon to drag in and these `steps`, App/PermissionGuide.swift). `turned_away.ask_again_minutes` is how long an item the account turned away (a 4xx about that item) waits before it is sent again, unless it changes first, since the account itself can change. `item_trouble` is for one item whose file the account would not keep (a 5xx saying the storage did not finish it): only that item waits, with `retry_seconds` doubling to `longest_seconds` and staying pending until its file is kept; transient service failures wait at the account level and never discard the file. `long_text` says how long an item's words may be before they go whole as a text file beside the item (`file_name` over the item's {title} and {route}), the item carrying their opening and `rest` (filled with {name} and {characters}). `read` says how what is new there reaches the person's AIs: `route` (the name it arrives under), `reader` (a leaf in read-new-items.mjs READERS; `sqlite` runs `query` against `store` with `:since` in `time` units, `folder` lists `store`), `text` (the words, a template over the values read), `group` (one item per window, per `by`), `preview_px` (pictures become a small preview; the picture stays on this Mac), `cursor` ("moves": read from the oldest item not yet sent; a grouped place from the start of that window), `from_person` (false when what arrives there was written by someone else, like Mail, so it reaches the AIs as information, never as the person's instructions; a query column named from_person decides it per item instead, as Mail's does: 1 only for a message in a Sent mailbox, since where Mail keeps a message cannot be faked the way a From address can) and `settle_seconds`. `every_seconds` is how often places are looked for, `look_seconds` how long one place may take to check (a child can start slowly or hold a read; a deadline says the place could not be checked, never that access was refused), `read_every_seconds` how often each place is read, `files_folder` where previews and recordings are kept in the person's files. Nothing written before a place was first read is sent. `readers_first` names the programs that take the reading over from any other program on the same computer, first one first: a reader counts as the app whose bundle carries its runtime (the Trillion Mac app runs it as its own child on the Node.js inside the app), so the one Full Disk Access switch a person turns on is Trillion's, and the helper reads only while the app is not running. Contacts are read by the list-people tool, not here. A row marked `runs_ais` (or in category AI) names an app the person's AIs run in, which no Mac hold ever closes (tools/hold-a-computer-quiet in the Workshop, handed these rows by computer/mac-tools.json `keep_open_rows`).

pace._what: How `every_seconds` and `read_every_seconds` follow what this computer is doing (pace.mjs). `sense` rows read one state each from a command's output (no shell): `map` turns the first captured text into the state's value, `threshold` compares the first captured number. `rows` are tried in order: the first whose `when` equals the sensed state sets the multiplier of both waits (a state that could not be sensed matches no `when` that names it). Idle is HIDIdleTime, in nanoseconds: 300000000000 is five minutes without a key or a mouse move. Retuning a pace is editing a row here.

hearing._why: First because it hears English meetings better and faster than mlx-whisper on the same Mac (measured 2026-10-21 on the same public AMI audio: meeting ES2004a, 17.5 min, 20.5% against 23.0% word error at 41x against 13x real time; 843 AMI test utterances, 8.9% against 15.9% at 21x against 6x; a 163 MB download against 1.6 GB). It needs 16 GB: with the Whisper model that finds the language it took 8.7 GB at its peak against mlx-whisper's 5.9 GB, so a Mac with 8 GB hears with mlx-whisper.. English only and unsteerable: hearWith (keep-drive-files.mjs) passes any other language, and any prompt, on to mlx-whisper; the program finds an unknown language with Whisper first.

read.query: SELECT m.guid AS source_id, m.date / 1000000000.0 AS at, COALESCE(c.guid, h.id, 'messages') AS conversation, COALESCE(NULLIF(c.display_name, ''), c.chat_identifier, h.id, 'someone') AS title, CASE WHEN m.is_from_me = 1 THEN 'Me' ELSE COALESCE(h.id, 'Them') END AS who, COALESCE(m.text, CASE WHEN m.cache_has_attachments = 1 THEN '(sent an attachment)' END) AS text, m.attributedBody AS body FROM message m LEFT JOIN handle h ON h.ROWID = m.handle_id LEFT JOIN chat_message_join j ON j.message_id = m.ROWID LEFT JOIN chat c ON c.ROWID = j.chat_id WHERE m.date > :since * 1000000000 AND m.associated_message_type = 0 AND m.item_type = 0

SELECT i.UUID AS source_id, i.last_modified AS at, i.summary AS title, COALESCE(i.summary, '(no title)') AS event, datetime(i.start_date + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS starts, datetime(i.end_date + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS ends, COALESCE(l.title, '') AS place, COALESCE(c.title, '') AS calendar, COALESCE(i.description, '') AS notes FROM CalendarItem i LEFT JOIN Location l ON l.ROWID = i.location_id LEFT JOIN Calendar c ON c.ROWID = i.calendar_id WHERE i.last_modified > :since

SELECT r.ZCKIDENTIFIER AS source_id, r.ZLASTMODIFIEDDATE AS at, r.ZTITLE AS title, CASE WHEN r.ZCOMPLETED = 1 THEN 'done' ELSE 'to do' END AS done, COALESCE(datetime(r.ZDUEDATE + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime'), 'no date') AS due, COALESCE(l.ZNAME, '') AS list, COALESCE(r.ZNOTES, '') AS notes FROM ZREMCDREMINDER r LEFT JOIN ZREMCDBASELIST l ON l.Z_PK = r.ZLIST WHERE r.ZLASTMODIFIEDDATE > :since AND COALESCE(r.ZMARKEDFORDELETION, 0) = 0 AND r.ZTITLE IS NOT NULL

SELECT m.ROWID AS source_id, m.date_received AS at, COALESCE(s.subject, '(no subject)') AS title, COALESCE(NULLIF(a.comment, '') || ' <' || a.address || '>', a.address, 'someone') AS sender, COALESCE(su.summary, '') AS summary, CASE WHEN mb.url LIKE '%/Sent%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS from_person FROM messages m LEFT JOIN addresses a ON a.ROWID = m.sender LEFT JOIN subjects s ON s.ROWID = m.subject LEFT JOIN summaries su ON su.ROWID = m.summary LEFT JOIN mailboxes mb ON mb.ROWID = m.mailbox WHERE m.date_received > :since AND m.deleted = 0 AND mb.url NOT LIKE '%Junk%' AND mb.url NOT LIKE '%Spam%' AND mb.url NOT LIKE '%Trash%' AND mb.url NOT LIKE '%Deleted%'

SELECT a.ZUUID AS source_id, a.ZADDEDDATE AS at, a.ZFILENAME AS title, CASE WHEN a.ZKIND = 1 THEN 'A video' WHEN a.ZKINDSUBTYPE = 10 THEN 'A screenshot' ELSE 'A photo' END AS kind, datetime(a.ZDATECREATED + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS taken, strftime('%Y-%m', a.ZDATECREATED + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS month, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H-%M-%S', a.ZDATECREATED + 978307200, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') AS stamp, substr(a.ZUUID, 1, 8) AS short, CASE WHEN a.ZLATITUDE BETWEEN -90 AND 90 AND a.ZLATITUDE != 0 THEN ' at ' || round(a.ZLATITUDE, 4) || ', ' || round(a.ZLONGITUDE, 4) ELSE '' END AS place, CASE WHEN a.ZKIND = 1 THEN NULL ELSE a.ZDIRECTORY END AS directory, CASE WHEN a.ZKIND = 1 THEN NULL ELSE a.ZFILENAME END AS filename, a.ZUUID AS uuid, a.ZKIND AS kind_code, a.ZDIRECTORY AS original_directory, a.ZFILENAME AS original_filename, substr(a.ZUUID, 1, 1) AS first FROM ZASSET a WHERE a.ZADDEDDATE > :since AND a.ZADDEDDATE < :before AND a.ZTRASHEDSTATE = 0 AND COALESCE(a.ZHIDDEN, 0) = 0 ORDER BY a.ZADDEDDATE DESC LIMIT :limit
